c.tagline: Monuments, marble, and the pulse of power.

emergency.note: 911 covers all emergencies; dial 311 for non-urgent city services.

hood_landmark.Georgetown: the C&O Canal and cobblestoned M Street, plus the famous 'Exorcist steps'
hood_landmark.Dupont Circle: the Dupont Circle fountain at the foot of Embassy Row
hood_landmark.Adams Morgan: 18th Street's mural-lined nightlife and dining strip
hood_landmark.Capitol Hill: the U.S. Capitol building and historic Eastern Market
hood_landmark.Shaw: the restored Howard Theatre, cradle of the city's Black music heritage

avoid.reason: Tourist core (Mall, Georgetown) safe; caution in parts of Southeast/Anacostia at night

hood_desc: Historic cobblestone streets, upscale boutiques and waterfront dining make Georgetown a polished, picturesque quarter that suits luxury travelers and shoppers, though it has no Metro station of its own.

An elegant, walkable district of embassies, tree-lined streets, bookstores and lively bars around a central fountain, Dupont Circle is ideal for young professionals, LGBTQ travelers and those wanting central nightlife.
A bohemian, multicultural nightlife hub packed with ethnic restaurants, dive bars and live music, Adams Morgan draws a younger, energetic crowd looking for an eclectic and affordable scene.

Home to the U.S. Capitol, charming rowhouses, Eastern Market and neighborhood pubs, Capitol Hill blends political power with a residential, family-friendly feel that appeals to history buffs and quieter stays.

A trendy, revitalized area with a rich Black cultural heritage, buzzing along the U Street corridor with jazz history, cocktail bars and hip restaurants, Shaw suits foodies and nightlife seekers wanting an authentic local vibe.

water.note: Tap water is treated and safe to drink.

transit.pay: Tap a contactless credit/debit card or phone directly at Metrorail faregates and bus readers (Tap. Ride. Go.), or use a SmarTrip card - $2 from station vending machines or free in Apple/Google Wallet. Rail fares run about $2.25-6.75 by distance and time of day; buses are a flat $2.25. The DC Streetcar on H Street is free.
transit.hours: Metrorail runs 5am-midnight Mon-Thu, until 1am Fri-Sat (from 7am weekends), and 7am-midnight Sun; several Metrobus routes run 24 hours.

food.name: Half-smoke
food.desc: DC's own half-pork, half-beef smoked sausage, split and griddled, then buried under chili, mustard and onions in a soft bun.

places.name: Ben's Chili Bowl
places.note: Serving the chili half-smoke since 1958; the definitive DC version and a civil-rights landmark.

places.name: DCity Smokehouse
places.note: Pitmaster-made half-smoke topped with pulled pork, slaw and crispy onions on the Big Snoop.

places.name: HalfSmoke
places.note: Modern take with build-your-own toppings, mustard slaw and bacon; lively bar scene.

food.name: Mumbo sauce wings
food.desc: Fried wings drenched in mumbo (mambo) sauce, DC's sweet-tangy red carryout condiment that locals guard like a family recipe.

places.name: Yum's II Carryout
places.note: Classic bulletproof-glass carryout widely cited as the mumbo sauce benchmark.

places.name: Henry's Soul Cafe
places.note: Longtime soul food counter; wings, sides and sweet potato pie worth the extra order.

places.name: Wingo's
places.note: Student-favorite wing shop with mumbo among a long sauce list; open late.

food.name: Doro wat with injera
food.desc: Slow-simmered berbere chicken stew with a hard-boiled egg, scooped up with spongy sour injera. DC has the largest Ethiopian community in the US.

places.name: Chercher Ethiopian Restaurant
places.note: Repeatedly named DC's best Ethiopian; makes and sells its own injera next door.

places.name: Dukem Ethiopian Restaurant
places.note: U Street institution with live music and generous combination platters.

places.name: Ethiopic
places.note: Polished dining room, strong vegetarian combo and a good Ethiopian wine list.

food.name: Chesapeake crab cake
food.desc: Jumbo lump blue crab bound with almost no filler and broiled, a Chesapeake Bay classic that DC kitchens treat as a point of pride.

places.name: Old Ebbitt Grill
places.note: Historic bar near the White House; crab cakes plus a busy raw bar and late oyster happy hour.

places.name: Hank's Oyster Bar
places.note: Neighborhood seafood mainstay from chef Jamie Leeds; New England-leaning menu.

places.name: Blue Duck Tavern
places.note: Refined jumbo lump crab cake with lemon-caper remoulade in a Michelin-recognized dining room.

food.name: Jumbo slice
food.desc: A paper-plate-defying pizza slice the size of your head, folded in half and eaten standing up on Adams Morgan's 18th Street after midnight.

places.name: Pizza Mart
places.note: The original jumbo slice window; queue forms after the bars close on 18th Street.

places.name: Duccini's Pizza
places.note: Rival jumbo slice shop a few doors down; locals argue it has the better crust.

food.name: Rickey
food.desc: DC's official native cocktail, invented here in the 1880s: rye or gin, half a lime squeezed and dropped in, topped with soda water.

places.name: Columbia Room
places.note: James Beard-winning cocktail bar; the place to drink a Rickey made with real care.

places.name: Off the Record
places.note: Red-leather bar under the Hay-Adams with political caricatures and classic drinks.

food.name: Ethiopian buna coffee
food.desc: Green beans roasted, ground and brewed in a clay jebena at your table, poured in three rounds with incense and popcorn alongside.

places.name: Sidamo Coffee and Tea
places.note: Runs a traditional Sunday coffee ceremony; roasts its own Ethiopian beans.

places.name: Chercher Ethiopian Restaurant
places.note: Order buna after the combination platter for the full jebena service.

landmarks: Lincoln Memorial

A neoclassical temple honoring the 16th president, its towering marble statue gazes out over the Reflecting Pool. The steps here have hosted some of the most iconic moments in American civil rights history.
United States Capitol
The gleaming white dome atop Capitol Hill is the beating heart of American democracy. Its rotunda and surrounding grounds offer some of the most photographed vistas in the nation's capital.
Washington Monument
This 555-foot marble obelisk has punctuated the D.C. skyline since 1884, honoring the nation's first president. Ride to the top for sweeping views across the National Mall.
The White House
The iconic residence and workplace of the U.S. president has stood at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue since 1800. Its stately North Portico is instantly recognizable the world over.
Jefferson Memorial
Set gracefully on the Tidal Basin, this domed rotunda is especially magical when framed by cherry blossoms each spring. It's one of the most romantic photo spots in the city.
National Mall
This grand grassy expanse links the Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial, flanked by world-class museums and monuments. It's the ceremonial and symbolic heart of the nation.
Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
Home to the legendary Hope Diamond and a dinosaur hall that dazzles visitors of all ages, this free museum is a Mall must-see. Its grand rotunda greets guests with a massive African bush elephant.
Vietnam Veterans Memorial
Maya Lin's haunting black granite wall, etched with over 58,000 names, is one of the most moving memorials in the world. Its reflective surface invites quiet contemplation.
Georgetown Waterfront
Cobblestone streets, historic rowhouses, and a lively Potomac riverfront make this D.C.'s most charming neighborhood. It's perfect for a scenic stroll and skyline photos.
Arlington National Cemetery

Just across the Potomac, rows of pristine white headstones stretch across rolling hills as a solemn tribute to fallen service members. The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier's changing of the guard is not to be missed.

train.note: No international trains serve Washington - the nearest cross-border services are Amtrak's Adirondack and Maple Leaf out of New York. Everything runs from Union Station at 50 Massachusetts Avenue NE, where Acela trains reach New York in under three hours and Northeast Regional trains continue to Boston, alongside long-distance routes south to Virginia, the Carolinas and Florida (the Floridian and Silver Meteor), west to Chicago on the Floridian and to Chicago via Charlottesville on the thrice-weekly Cardinal. Acela fares climb sharply as departure nears, so book early; Northeast Regional and the Virginia state-supported trains are considerably cheaper. MARC and VRE commuter trains cover Baltimore, Frederick and northern Virginia, mostly on weekdays only.

bus.note: No direct international coaches - reaching Canada by bus means changing in New York. The main long-distance operators are Greyhound (https://www.greyhound.com/), FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/), Megabus (https://us.megabus.com/) and Peter Pan (https://peterpanbus.com/), using the Union Station Bus Terminal on the upper deck of the station garage plus curbside stops nearby. New York takes about 4.5 hours, Philadelphia 3 and Richmond 2. Advance online fares on the New York corridor can be a few dollars, but rise steeply on Friday and Sunday afternoons.

intl.to: Old Town Alexandria, Georgetown & National Harbor (USA) - from The Wharf in southwest DC

ferry.note: No international or intercity ferries. City Cruises' Potomac water taxi links The Wharf with Georgetown, Old Town Alexandria and National Harbor, with departures every 30-60 minutes from late morning; the Alexandria hop takes about half an hour and is a genuine way to cross the river, though the timetable thins out sharply in winter. Tickets are sold online and at the dock, and season passes are available for regular users.

half.name: Harpers Ferry

half.name: Annapolis
half.blurb: Maryland's charming waterfront capital, known for sailing, seafood, and its colonial Naval Academy.

half.name: Mount Vernon
half.blurb: George Washington's riverside estate, a preserved plantation home with gardens along the Potomac.

half.name: Baltimore
half.blurb: A lively harbor city offering a revitalized waterfront, aquarium, and rich maritime history.

half.name: Richmond
half.blurb: Virginia's historic capital, blending Civil War landmarks with riverfront parks and creative dining.
